reasoning: The defect is real. In register_jit_udf (haversine.py:121-137), func_p is created at L125 via duckdb_create_scalar_function(). The DuckDB C API contract (confirmed by examples.md:95-96 and the finding notes) is that duckdb_register_scalar_function copies the scalar function into the catalog; the caller retains ownership of the original builder handle and must call duckdb_destroy_scalar_function on it regardless of outcome. The destroy call at L136-137 sits AFTER the assert at L135. If duckdb_register_scalar_function returns DuckDBError, the assert fires and L136-137 never execute, leaking func_p. The pattern is consistent across the codebase (test/test_ducklib.py:1960-1964 confirms destroy-after-register is the expected caller discipline), making the ordering error clear. The DOUBLE logical type (dbl_p) is not leaked: it is correctly destroyed at L131-132 before register, which is safe because add_parameter/set_return_type copy the logical type by value into the function object per the C API contract. Severity low is appropriate: registration cannot realistically fail in this specific example (fixed name, fresh in-memory connection), so the leak is latent here. The concern that haversine.py is the de-facto reference pattern for JIT scalar-UDF registration is valid — downstream callers copying this pattern into a long-lived connection with re-registration (e.g. name collision) would leak one builder handle per failed attempt.
